name: KR Reykjavík
content:
Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur (commonly known as KR Reykjavík) is the oldest football club in Iceland, founded in 1899 in the capital city Reykjavík. It plays in the top division of Icelandic football and has been a central part of the country’s football development since the early 20th century. The club won the first-ever Icelandic championship in 1912, establishing itself as an early dominant force.

KR is widely regarded as the most successful club in Icelandic football history. It has won the national league title more than 25 times and holds the record for Icelandic Cup victories, with 14 titles. The club was also a pioneer internationally, becoming the first Icelandic team to compete in European competitions in the 1960s. Its long history includes multiple periods of success, including notable title wins in 1999 and the early 21st century.

The club plays its home matches at KR-völlur in Reykjavík and is known for its traditional black-and-white colors. Beyond football, it operates as a multi-sport organization with various departments. KR remains a key institution in Icelandic sports, contributing to player development and maintaining a strong presence in both domestic and international competitions.

name: KR Reykjavík B
content:
KR Reykjavík B was the reserve team of Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur, one of Iceland’s oldest and most successful football clubs. As a second team, it primarily consisted of younger players and squad members who were developing or not regularly featuring in the first team. Despite its status, the team occasionally competed in national competitions, including the Icelandic Cup.

The most notable achievement of KR Reykjavík B came in 1968, when the team made an unexpected and historic run to the final of the Icelandic Cup. This was a rare accomplishment for a reserve side, as it required defeating several established first-division clubs along the way. Their cup run drew significant attention in Icelandic football due to its unusual nature and competitive performance.

In the final, KR Reykjavík B ultimately fell short and finished as runners-up. Even though they did not win the trophy, their achievement remains one of the most remarkable moments for a reserve team in Icelandic football history. After this period, reserve teams gradually became less prominent in major domestic cup competitions.

name: Valur
content:
Valur is one of the most prominent football clubs in Iceland, based in Reykjavík and founded in 1911 as part of a multi-sport organization. The men’s football team competes in the top tier of Icelandic football and plays its home matches at Hlíðarendi. Known for its red and white colors, the club has spent the vast majority of its history in the top division and is considered one of the traditional powerhouses of Icelandic football.

Valur achieved its first major success by winning the Icelandic championship in 1930, and it went on to build a strong legacy with multiple title-winning periods throughout the 20th century. The club has won the national league 23 times, making it one of the most successful teams in the country. In addition to league titles, Valur has also secured numerous domestic cup victories, reinforcing its status as a consistently competitive side in Icelandic football.

In recent years, Valur has remained a key contender in domestic competitions, winning the league as recently as 2020. The club continues to evolve through managerial changes and notable player signings, aiming to maintain its competitive edge. With a long-standing tradition and strong infrastructure, Valur plays an important role in Iceland’s football scene and regularly participates in European qualifying competitions.

name: Fram Reykjavík
content:
Knattspyrnufélagið Fram, commonly known as Fram Reykjavík, is one of the oldest and most historic football clubs in Iceland, founded in 1908 in Reykjavík. It is a multi-sport organization, but its football team is the most prominent section. The club originally operated near the city center before relocating to the Úlfarsárdalur district, where it is now based. Fram currently competes in the top tier of Icelandic football after earning promotion in 2021.

Fram is considered one of the most successful clubs in Icelandic football history, having won 18 national league titles and multiple domestic cups. The club enjoyed its greatest dominance in the early decades of Icelandic football and again during the 1980s and early 1990s. Known for its blue and white colors, Fram has played an important role in shaping the development of the sport in Iceland and has long been regarded as one of the country’s traditional powerhouse teams.

Although the club has experienced periods of relegation and rebuilding in the 21st century, it has consistently returned to the top division and remains competitive. Fram has also participated in European competitions and is notable for facing major clubs such as Real Madrid in continental tournaments. With a strong legacy and continued presence in Icelandic football, the club remains an important part of the national sporting landscape.

name: ÍA Akranes
content:
Íþróttabandalag Akraness (commonly known as ÍA Akranes) is an Icelandic multi-sport club founded in 1946 and based in the town of Akranes on the west coast of Iceland. The organization includes several sports, but its football team is the most prominent and widely recognized. The club plays its home matches at Akranesvöllur and is traditionally associated with yellow and black colors.

The football team is one of the most successful in Icelandic history, having won 18 national league titles and 9 Icelandic Cups. ÍA enjoyed particularly strong periods of dominance in the mid-20th century and again during the 1990s, when it secured multiple championships. The club has consistently been known for its competitiveness and its ability to perform at the highest domestic level.

In addition to its success, ÍA is recognized for its strong youth development system, producing many notable Icelandic players who have gone on to represent the national team and play internationally. Although the club has experienced fluctuations in performance in recent years, it remains an important and historic institution in Icelandic football, with a lasting impact on the sport in the country.

name: FH Hafnarfjarðar
content:
FH (Fimleikafélag Hafnarfjarðar) is an Icelandic football club based in Hafnarfjörður and part of a larger multi-sport organization founded in 1929. The men’s football team itself was established later and currently competes in the top tier of Icelandic football. The club plays its home matches at Kaplakriki stadium and is known for its white and black colors.

FH became one of the dominant forces in Icelandic football in the early 21st century. The club won its first national championship in 2004 and quickly established a period of success, securing multiple league titles in the following years. Overall, FH has won the Icelandic championship eight times, along with several domestic cups and league cups, making it one of the most successful modern-era teams in the country.

The team has also participated in European competitions and is known for its consistent performances in domestic tournaments. Despite fluctuations in form in recent seasons, FH remains a competitive side in Icelandic football and continues to play an important role in the development of the sport in Hafnarfjörður and across the country.

name: Víkingur Reykjavík
content:
Knattspyrnufélagið Víkingur, commonly known as Víkingur Reykjavík, is one of the oldest sports clubs in Iceland, founded in 1908 and based in the Fossvogur area of Reykjavík. Originally established as a football club, it has since developed into a multi-sport organization with several departments, although football remains its most prominent section. The team plays its home matches at Víkingsvöllur and competes in the top tier of Icelandic football.

Víkingur has a long and successful history in Icelandic football, winning multiple national league titles and domestic cups. The club experienced early success in the 1920s and later enjoyed strong periods in the 1980s and early 1990s. In recent years, it has re-emerged as a dominant force, winning league titles in 2021, 2023, and 2025, along with several Icelandic Cup victories, marking one of the most successful eras in its history.

The club is also known for developing talented players who have gone on to represent Iceland internationally and play abroad. With its modern resurgence, strong squad, and stable management, Víkingur continues to be a leading club in Icelandic football and a regular participant in European competitions, reinforcing its status as a major force in the domestic game.

name: Keflavík
content:
Knattspyrnudeild Keflavíkur, commonly known as Keflavík, is an Icelandic football club founded in 1929 and based in the town of Reykjanesbær. It is part of the multi-sport organization Keflavík ÍF and plays its home matches at Keflavíkurvöllur. The team has been a regular participant in Icelandic league football since the mid-20th century and often competes in the country’s top divisions.

Keflavík enjoyed its greatest success during the 1960s and early 1970s, when it won four national league titles in 1964, 1969, 1971, and 1973. The club has also claimed four Icelandic Cup victories, with its first coming in 1975 and additional wins in later decades. Over time, the team has moved between the top and second tiers but has largely remained a consistent presence in Icelandic football.

In addition to domestic success, Keflavík has participated in European competitions, facing well-known clubs such as Ferencváros, Everton, Tottenham Hotspur, and Real Madrid. The club is recognized for its role in developing football in its region and continues to compete at a high level, maintaining its status as an important and historic team in Icelandic football.

name: ÍBV Vestmannaeyjar
content:
ÍBV (Íþróttabandalag Vestmannaeyja) is an Icelandic football club based in Vestmannaeyjar, founded in 1903 as part of a multi-sport organization. The men’s football team competes in the top tier of Icelandic football and plays its home matches at Hásteinsvöllur. As one of the notable clubs outside Reykjavík, ÍBV has long represented the Westman Islands in national competitions.

The club has achieved success at the domestic level, winning the Icelandic championship three times in 1979, 1997, and 1998. In addition, ÍBV has secured five Icelandic Cup titles, with victories spanning several decades. These achievements highlight periods of strong performance, particularly in the late 20th century when the club established itself among the top teams in Iceland.

ÍBV has also competed in European tournaments, gaining experience against international opposition. The club is known for developing talented players and maintaining a competitive presence in Icelandic football despite fluctuations in league performance. With its strong local identity and historical success, ÍBV remains an important part of the country’s football landscape.

name: Breiðablik
content:
Breiðablik is an Icelandic football club based in Kópavogur and founded in 1950 as part of the larger Breiðablik multi-sport organization. The men’s football team competes in the top division of Icelandic football and plays its home matches at Kópavogsvöllur. The club is widely known for its strong emphasis on youth development and its modern, possession-based style of play, which has helped it become one of the most respected teams in the country.

Historically, Breiðablik spent many years moving between divisions before establishing itself as a consistent top-flight club in the 21st century. Its first major breakthrough came with winning the Icelandic Cup in 2009, followed by its first league championship in 2010. Since then, the club has grown into a regular contender for domestic titles and has won multiple league championships in recent seasons, marking a strong era of success.

On the European stage, Breiðablik has also made history by becoming the first Icelandic men’s team to reach the group stage of a UEFA competition. This achievement highlighted the club’s progress and development in international football. Today, Breiðablik remains one of Iceland’s leading clubs, known for producing talent, competing consistently at the top level, and representing Iceland in European tournaments.

name: KA Akureyri
content:
Knattspyrnufélag Akureyrar (KA) is an Icelandic sports club based in Akureyri, founded in 1928. The men’s football team is one of the main sections of the multi-sport organization and competes in Iceland’s top football division. The club plays its home matches at Akureyrarvöllur and is traditionally associated with blue and yellow colours. It has a long-standing rivalry with local club Þór Akureyri, which is a defining feature of football in the region.

The club’s greatest historical achievement came in 1989 when KA won the Icelandic championship for the first time in its history after a dramatic title race. This remains their only league title, but it is considered one of the most memorable moments in Icelandic football history. KA has also achieved success in domestic cup competitions, including winning the Icelandic Cup in 2024, showing its ability to compete at the top level in different eras.

In addition to domestic success, KA has participated in European competitions, representing Akureyri on the international stage. The club has experienced periods of both strength and inconsistency, moving between divisions at times, but it has remained an important part of Icelandic football. Today, KA continues to compete in the top division and contributes significantly to the sporting identity of northern Iceland.

name: Stjarnan
content:
Stjarnan is an Icelandic sports club based in Garðabær, founded in 1960, with its men’s football section competing in the top tier of Icelandic football. The team plays its home matches at Samsung völlurinn and is known for its blue and white colours. The club is part of a larger multi-sport organisation that also includes basketball, handball, volleyball, and gymnastics.

Stjarnan gradually rose through the Icelandic football system and established itself in the top division in the late 2000s. Its breakthrough came in 2014 when the club won its first Icelandic league championship after an unbeaten season, equalling the points record in the process. This success marked the beginning of its status as one of the strongest teams in the country.

The club has also gained attention in European competitions, reaching qualifying rounds of UEFA tournaments and achieving notable victories against stronger opposition. In addition to its sporting success, Stjarnan became internationally famous for its creative and humorous goal celebrations, which spread widely online. Today, it remains a competitive and well-known club in Icelandic football.

name: Fylkir
content:
Fylkir is an Icelandic sports club based in the Árbær district of Reykjavík, founded on 28 May 1967. The men’s football team is one of the club’s main departments and competes in the top tiers of Icelandic football. The club plays its home matches at Fylkisvöllur and is traditionally associated with orange and black colours. It was originally established by young local players with a strong focus on community and youth development.

Fylkir spent much of its early history moving between divisions before gradually establishing itself in the top flight. The club reached the top division for the first time in the late 1980s and became more stable in the late 1990s. One of its most successful periods came in the early 2000s, when it finished near the top of the league and won the Icelandic Cup twice in a row in 2001 and 2002.

In European competitions, Fylkir has competed in qualifiers for UEFA tournaments, gaining experience against stronger international clubs. Although it has not become a dominant force in Icelandic football, the club has produced several notable players and remains an important part of Reykjavík’s football culture. Today, Fylkir continues to compete at a professional level while maintaining its strong local identity and emphasis on player development.

name: ÍBA Akureyri
content:
ÍB Akureyri (Íþróttabandalag Akureyrar, often abbreviated ÍBA) was a football club based in Akureyri in northern Iceland. It was formed as a joint team representing the town’s main sports clubs, primarily KA and Þór, with the aim of combining local talent into a single competitive side. The club became an important symbol of cooperation in Icelandic sport during the mid-20th century.

The team competed in Iceland’s top football division for many seasons and achieved solid results without ever winning the national league title. Its strongest period came in the 1960s, when ÍB Akureyri consistently finished near the top of the table and reached its peak competitive level. The club also won the Icelandic Cup in 1969, which remains its most significant trophy.

In addition to domestic competitions, ÍB Akureyri also represented Iceland in European tournaments, though with limited success. In 1974, the cooperation between KA and Þór ended, leading to the dissolution of the combined team. After that, both clubs resumed competing separately, and ÍB Akureyri ceased to exist as a unified football identity.

name: Fjölnir
content:
Ungmennafélagið Fjölnir is an Icelandic multi-sport club based in the Grafarvogur district of Reykjavík, founded in 1988. The football section is one of its main departments and has become the club’s most visible competitive branch. Fjölnir was created to represent the growing suburban community in northern Reykjavík and quickly developed into a structured sports organization with several athletic divisions.

The men’s football team has spent most of its history moving between Iceland’s top two divisions. One of its key achievements came in 2013 when the club won the second tier and earned promotion to the top division, marking a major milestone in its development. Since then, Fjölnir has alternated between promotion battles and relegation struggles, reflecting its status as a competitive but developing club in Icelandic football.

Beyond results on the pitch, Fjölnir is known as a broad community sports club with multiple disciplines, including basketball, handball, and other sports alongside football. Its structure emphasizes youth development and participation across the local area, making it an important part of Reykjavík’s sporting landscape. The football team continues to aim for stability in the top divisions while building on its academy and community-based identity.

name: Grindavík
content:
Grindavík is an Icelandic football club based in the town of Grindavík in the southwest of the country. The men’s football team is part of the Ungmennafélag Grindavíkur sports association, founded in 1935. The club plays its home matches at Grindavíkurvöllur and traditionally wears yellow and blue colours. It has long been an important representative of the small coastal community in national football.

The club spent many years working its way up through the Icelandic football league system, reaching the top division in the 1990s. After establishing itself in the top tier, Grindavík experienced periods of stability but was also relegated for the first time in 2006. Since then, the team has moved between divisions, with promotions and relegations shaping much of its modern history.

Grindavík has had notable achievements, including winning the Icelandic League Cup in 2000 and producing strong individual performances such as Andri Rúnar Bjarnason becoming league top scorer in 2017. In recent years, the club has also been affected by natural disasters in the region, which have disrupted its activities, but it continues to compete and represent its community in Icelandic football.

name: Leiftur
content:
Íþróttafélagið Leiftur was an Icelandic football club based in Ólafsfjörður in northern Iceland. The club was founded in 1981 and represented a small coastal community, becoming one of the more notable teams from rural Iceland to reach the national football system. Leiftur played its home matches in Ólafsfjörður and later also used facilities in nearby towns when competing at higher levels.

The club rose through the Icelandic league system during the 1990s, reaching the top division and establishing itself as a competitive side despite its small population base. Leiftur’s strongest period came in the late 1990s, when it regularly competed in the top tier and achieved solid league results. It also gained attention for taking part in European competitions after qualifying through its domestic performances.

In the early 2000s, Leiftur merged with another local club to form Leiftur/Dalvík, aiming to strengthen football in the region. However, the combined project did not maintain long-term top-level stability, and the original club identity eventually faded from the top divisions. Despite this, Leiftur remains remembered as an important part of northern Iceland’s football history and one of the smaller clubs that briefly reached the national spotlight.

name: Víðir
content:
Knattspyrnufélagið Víðir is an Icelandic football club based in Garður on the Reykjanes Peninsula. The club was founded in 1936 and has traditionally represented a small coastal community in Icelandic football. It plays its home matches at Nesfisk-völlurinn and has been an important local sports institution for decades.

The men’s team has spent several periods competing in the higher tiers of Icelandic football, including appearances in the top division during the mid-1980s and early 1990s. One of its most notable achievements was reaching the Icelandic Cup final in 1987, where the club finished as runner-up after facing Fram. These years marked the peak of Víðir’s competitive success on a national level.

Outside its top-flight spells, Víðir has frequently moved between divisions, winning lower-tier championships and rebuilding its squad over time. The club remains closely tied to its local community and is known for developing regional talent. Despite not being a consistent top-tier side, it holds an important place in Icelandic football history as one of the smaller clubs to reach national prominence.

name: Þór Akureyri
content:
Þór Akureyri is an Icelandic multi-sport club based in Akureyri, founded in 1915. The men’s football team is one of the main departments of the club and represents the northern city in Icelandic football competitions. It plays its home matches at Þórsvöllur and traditionally wears white and red colours. The club is one of the two major football institutions in Akureyri, alongside KA, and the rivalry between them is a key part of local football culture.

The football team has spent much of its history moving between divisions in Iceland. While it has not become a dominant top-flight club, it has regularly competed in the upper tiers, earning promotions and fighting to maintain its place in the higher leagues. One of its most notable achievements was reaching the Icelandic Cup final in 2011, where it finished as runner-up after a strong cup run.

Þór has also been part of important football moments in Akureyri, including the period when the city fielded a combined team with KA in earlier decades. Today, it continues to compete professionally and focuses on maintaining stability in the national league system while developing local players and strengthening its role in northern Icelandic football.

name: ÍF Vestri
content:
Vestri is an Icelandic football club based in Ísafjörður in the Westfjords region. It is part of the larger multi-sport organization Íþróttafélagið Vestri, which was formed in 2016 through the merger of several local sports clubs, including the football side that eventually became Vestri’s men’s team. The club represents one of the main sporting identities in the remote northwestern part of Iceland.

The football section has its roots in 1986, originally founded as BÍ (Boltafélag Ísafjarðar). Over time, the club went through several reorganizations and mergers, most notably a cooperation with Bolungarvík between 2006 and 2016. After the formation of Íþróttafélagið Vestri in 2016, the team continued under its current name and structure, gradually strengthening its position in Icelandic football.

In recent years, Vestri has progressed steadily through the Icelandic league system, reaching higher divisions and establishing itself in national competitions. The club achieved a historic milestone by earning promotion to the top tier, marking a major achievement for a team from a small and geographically isolated region. Vestri is now recognized for its strong community identity and growing competitiveness in Icelandic football.
